facts.text: The word 'Manitou' comes from an Algonquian term meaning 'spirit'—the town was named for the spiritual energy believed to inhabit the mineral springs.
William Abraham Bell founded Manitou Springs in 1872 as a scenic health resort, drawing tuberculosis patients to its thin mountain air and sparkling water.
In 1980, the Manitou Springs Historic District was created, becoming one of the country’s largest National Historic Districts on the National Register of Historic Places.
By the 1890s the town boasted seven grand hotels—including the Cliff House, Barker House, and Grandview—alongside a bustling bathhouse that welcomed visitors.
Olympic athletes use Manitou Springs for altitude training, taking advantage of its high elevation and crisp air.
